title: 11 Things Teachers Should Say No To
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin frames saying no more often as one of the fastest, easiest levers a teacher has for reducing chronic stress, and organizes the piece around eleven specific categories of demands on a teacher's time and energy worth declining: gossip, academic favors for colleagues, over-helping students individually, optional administrator requests, extra committees, overly familiar parent relationships, planning-time interruptions, idle hallway conversations, excessive lesson planning, happy hour, and inconsistency in enforcing rules. Beyond simply listing these, he frames the underlying logic explicitly -- boundary-setting isn't selfish but selfless, since a teacher operating at their best is a greater benefit to students and colleagues than one who is depleted from overcommitment. He predicts the process will involve some initial discomfort and awkward moments in enforcing new boundaries, but argues that people ultimately respect boundaries once they're set, and closes by urging teachers to build their own personalized 'no' list rather than treating his eleven items as exhaustive.
points: Saying no more often is presented as one of the fastest, lowest-effort ways to substantially cut chronic teacher stress.
Specific targets include gossip, doing academic favors that let colleagues leech off your planning, and over-helping individual students at the expense of whole-class instruction.
Draw a hard line on parent relationships to avoid friendship or special favors, which in turn causes most parents to leave you alone to do your job.
Reframes boundary-setting as selfless rather than selfish: a teacher operating at their best is more valuable to students than one stretched thin.
Enforcing new boundaries will involve some initial discomfort, but people ultimately respect them once set.
quotes: Stress is crushing teachers, but there are things you can do to alleviate it. In fact, with a comprehensive approach, you can all but eliminate it.
But one of the quickest and easiest things you can do to put a substantial dent in the amount of stress you’re feeling is to say “no” more often.
It can feel like an escape, but gossiping about students or colleagues is distracting, time-consuming, and risks exposing yourself to excessive drama.
It’s good to share, but it’s not okay for colleagues to take advantage of your kindness by leeching off your hard work and planning .
It’s selfless because only when you’re at your best can you be a benefit to others.
Furthermore, you’ll discover that when you put boundaries on your time and attention, and focus more on what matters most, people will respect you for it.
